transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you. Could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hello, Dr. Smith. It is very nice to meet you, too. Thank you for taking the time to see me. Um, well, I hope I'm explaining this right, and I really don't want to be a bother to anyone. My husband thought it would be a good idea for me to come in and talk, and I always try to do what's best. 

It's just... well, it's a family matter, mostly. I really hate to speak ill of people, I truly do, but it's about my husband's sister. She's been working our family business, and... well, I don't want to sound like a complainer, but she's doing it so she can get control of the money. She's been trying to push me completely out of the decisions. 

I know folks in the family keep trying to smooth it all over and make it seem like it's nothing, but... well, I know what I've been seeing. It's been going on for more than a year now. Does that make sense? I hope I'm not sounding unreasonable to you.
Can you tell me what specific actions or evidence have you seen that lead you to believe she is trying to take control of the money?

Oh, goodness. Well... I suppose when you ask for actual evidence, I... I don't really have anything like paperwork or a list of things she's done. I'd feel just terrible keeping tabs on family like that, you know? That's not the kind of person I am, I really try to see the best in folks. 

It's just... well, I don't really have specific actions I can point to right this second. It's more of just knowing how things have shifted, but I haven't been gathering proof or anything. I'm so sorry, I know you probably need hard facts and examples, and I really don't want to be difficult or sound like I'm just making a fuss over nothing. I hope it's okay that I don't have a better answer for you. Am I making any sense at all?
Do you find yourself feeling this same way about other people in your life, such as friends, coworkers, or neighbors, or is this feeling strictly limited to your husband's sister?

Oh, goodness, no. No, um... I really hope you don't think I'm the sort of person who goes around having trouble with everyone. I get along just fine with my neighbors, and I have some lovely friends. 

It's strictly just... well, just my husband's sister. I really try my very best to be a good person and get along with folks, so I don't have these kinds of worries about anyone else at all. I'd just hate for you to think I'm a suspicious person by nature, because I'm truly, truly not. I always try to give people the benefit of the doubt. 

Is it okay that it's just limited to her? I hope I'm answering your questions right, I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need.
Have you ever heard voices or sounds that other people around you couldn't hear?

Oh, my, no. No, I've never experienced anything like that. I've heard about folks who go through that sort of thing, and my heart just goes out to them, it really does. But no, I don't hear anything that isn't really there. 

I really hope my talking about my sister-in-law didn't make you think I was... well, you know, really unwell in that way. I'm just a normal person going through a tough family situation, I promise. I don't hear voices or anything like that. Does that help? I really want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Is it possible that your interpretation of your sister-in-law's actions might be incorrect, or are you certain that she is intentionally trying to push you out of the business?

Oh, goodness... well, I know you're just doing your job by asking that, and I really appreciate how thorough you are. I know it must sound like I'm just being stubborn, and I'd hate for you to think I'm unreasonable or unwilling to look at things differently. I really try to be open-minded, I do.

But... well, I've been watching this happen for more than a year now. I came in because she's been working this family business in a way to get control of the money and push me out of all the decisions. And I know folks try to smooth it over and tell me I'm misunderstanding, but... I just know what I've been seeing. I'm so sorry if that makes me sound difficult. I don't mean to be. But I am certain about what she's doing. Is it okay that I feel that way? I hope I'm not frustrating you by not backing down on this.
Do you feel that other people, perhaps friends or family members, are working together with your sister-in-law to help her push you out of the business?

Oh, no, no, definitely not. I really don't think anyone else is involved. I mean, my husband and the rest of the family, they're all just trying to keep the peace, you know? They don't see what she's doing, but they certainly aren't helping her do it. 

I really wouldn't want you to think I'm the sort of person who believes everyone is out to get me. It's truly just her. I know she's acting alone in this. I hope that makes sense? I just want to make sure I'm giving you a clear picture of things without sounding like I'm accusing the whole family, because I'm definitely not.
Do you feel that your sister-in-law is using any secret codes, hidden signals, or unusual technology to communicate her intentions or to manipulate the business situation?

Oh, my goodness, no. No, nothing like that at all. I know you have to ask those sorts of things to be thorough, and I think it's wonderful how careful you are, but... well, I'd never claim something so, you know, out there. She's not using secret codes or spy gadgets or anything strange like that. 

It's just regular paperwork and bank accounts, just... doing things behind my back the normal way. I really wouldn't want you to think I'm the kind of person who makes up wild, science-fiction stories. I just want to be completely honest with you, and honestly, there's no secret signals or anything. Does that make sense? I hope I'm being helpful and answering everything the way you need me to.
When you think about the situation with your sister-in-law, do you ever find that your thoughts become disorganized or that you have trouble keeping your focus on one train of thought?

Oh, no, I don't think so. I mean, I know I might get a little flustered when I'm upset about the business, but my thoughts are perfectly clear. I can always keep my train of thought, and I know exactly what I'm saying. 

I'd hate for you to think my mind is slipping or that I'm getting confused. I really try to stay organized and keep track of everything, especially with all this going on. I hope I've been making sense today? I try very hard to speak clearly and stay on topic so I don't waste your time. Am I doing okay with that?
When you think about the situation with your sister-in-law, do you find yourself becoming intensely angry or irritable?

Oh, no... no, I wouldn't say intensely angry. I mean, I guess anyone would be a little bothered by the situation, but I'm really not an angry person at all. I don't fly off the handle or, you know, snap at people. I just try to handle things as calmly as I can. 

I'd really hate for you to think I'm... well, bitter, or difficult to be around. I try very hard to be pleasant and keep my emotions in check, even when things are stressful with the business. I hope that's okay? I just want to assure you that I'm not letting it turn me into a mean or irritable person. Am I explaining that alright?
Have you noticed any changes in your daily routine, such as becoming more withdrawn from your usual activities or struggling to take care of your personal grooming?

Oh, no, definitely not. I still get up every morning and make sure I look presentable. I know how important it is to keep up appearances, especially when things are a little stressful. I would never just... let myself go or hide away in my room. That's just not me. 

I still do all my usual things—keeping the house tidy, running my errands. I really try to stay on top of everything so nobody has to worry about me. I'd be so embarrassed if anyone thought I wasn't taking care of myself properly. I hope you can tell I'm trying my best to stay active and put together? I just want to make sure I'm doing all the right things.
